conventions.convention: Developments solve one fixed covariant coupled model with complete smooth matter data, not merely matching stress projections. The actual local existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses must apply at every restart. Dust velocity is prescribed and matched even at zero density.
The second fundamental form is K(V,W)=g(∇_V n,W), using the future unit normal. An orientation-preserving map preserves future cones; it need not carry the arbitrary representing field N to N′.

A development embedding maps the smaller development diffeomorphically onto an open subset of the larger one. Maximality means that every development of the same complete data embeds into the maximal development.

Common subdevelopments are realized inside the first ambient development. Correspondence requires an interior witness for every pair of ambient boundary neighborhoods; corresponding points have matching sides of the initial surface.
The smooth extension preserves metric, matter and connection on U together with the corresponding boundary set. No exterior isometry is asserted.

Time separation τ_q(r) measures future causal length from r to q. Empty competitor sets have supremum zero; r=q has a constant degenerate geodesic by convention, outside the nonzero-velocity causal-curve class.

Restart tubes use variable smooth positive widths with explicit derivative bounds. Radial overlap segments exclude a possibly boundary base; past-side geometry retains the original time orientation and matter data.

The dense-set recursion includes both future and past timelike rational vectors, retains each tangent basis after its first selection, and starts at D₀. The basis uses all admissible rational translated tangent balls.
Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are explicit mathematical premises. The physics conclusion is conditional on adopted model postulates and contains no measured inputs or observational inference.

load_bearing.statement: A development is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold solving the fixed coupled equations, with a spacelike Cauchy embedding inducing the prescribed complete data. Admissibility includes applicability of the supplied complete-data local existence and geometric uniqueness theorem at each actual spacelike restart.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. If a common subdevelopment of two developments of the same data contains every common subdevelopment with the same restricted map, its set C of corresponding boundary points is empty.

Under the stated Countable Choice and Dependent Choice hypotheses, every future causal segment in M with both endpoints in an open subdevelopment U sharing the initial Cauchy surface is contained in U.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the corresponding set C is relatively open in ∂U. The common map has a smooth neighborhood extension, locally invertible on U∪C, preserving metric, matter and connection there; its restriction to an embedded submanifold of U∪C is an embedding preserving the stated induced data and finite-order covariant derivatives.

Under its exact exposed-point, normal-neighborhood, diamond and localization hypotheses, the maximizing positive time-separation level component is a nonempty smooth spacelike hypersurface meeting the corresponding boundary. Quantitatively thin radial tubes preserve the original Cauchy property of U∪N and give overlap agreement with a future local isometry agreeing on the restart surface.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, a nonempty past corresponding-boundary set admits the stated exposure, localization, whole spacelike restart surface and quantitatively thin tubes, with the original Cauchy and overlap conclusions, without reversing any model field, future normal or complete data.
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Two developments of the same data have a unique common subdevelopment containing every common subdevelopment, with agreement of its map on each.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Gluing two developments of the same data along their maximal common development produces a Hausdorff second countable smooth development into which both embed by data-fixing development embeddings.

For the fixed complete admissible data, assuming Countable Choice, Dependent Choice, actual restart applicability and at least one development, the set-sized canonical family has a Hausdorff second countable smooth quotient development admitting a data-fixing development embedding from every development of those data.

Conditional on the supplied quotient Q and countable dense D, Countable Choice supplies tangent bases, and the images of all rational translated tangent balls on which the exponential is a diffeomorphism form a countable basis. The development suppliers' Dependent Choice hypotheses are retained.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, connected smooth complete constrained data of one fixed admissible coupled model, at least one development, and actual local uniqueness/restart applicability have a connected maximal globally hyperbolic development, unique up to exactly one data-fixing isometry.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.1 says that σ≪x≤q, 'with σ≠q or σ=q', 'in either case' relates two distinct points of Σ. When σ=q, the endpoints on Σ are equal. That branch instead contradicts causality through q≪x≤q. Causality is already available in L1, so this is a short proof correction rather than a defect in the compactness claim.

Proof step 4.1 has a justification group immediately after its opening sentence, followed on the next line by the rest of the same step and another final justification group. The complete step should be one paragraph with its tags only at the end.

Proof steps 2.1 and 3.2 each place a justification group before their argument is complete, then continue across several source lines and end with another group. These violate the required complete-step paragraph and trailing-tag layout.

The page says ex-gr-flat-restart-level-set 'checks the structural clauses' of the restart lemma. The example verifies the flat separation level's smoothness, spacelikeness, single-crossing property and radial segments; it does not instantiate the exposed common boundary, compact diamond or quantitative tube hypotheses and conclusions. The page description should identify the particular clauses illustrated.

alerts.finding: Clause (e) defines H⁺(S)=D⁺(S)\I⁻(D⁺(S)), then describes its points as 'not chronologically preceded by any point of D⁺(S)'. Membership outside I⁻(D⁺(S)) instead means that the point does not chronologically precede any point of D⁺(S). The displayed formula and its verbal explanation have opposite directions.

Statement (b) says '[0,n]⊆I_k for every k once n is fixed' and gives I_k=[0,b_k] with b_k→∞ as an example. That example supplies containment only for sufficiently large k for each fixed n. Proof step 7.1 correctly uses eventual containment and discards finitely many indices. The Statement should express that same quantifier.

seams_checked.note: The consumers retain complete initialization, recovery, fixed-model comparison and actual restart applicability. Scalar and strict-fluid restrictions are retained; nonnegative tilted dust uses its separate reduction and prescribed zero-density velocity.

Smooth boundaryless Lorentzian four-manifolds, signature −+++, metric-selected connection and future-cone preservation are used consistently. Representing orientation fields are not incorrectly required to coincide.

The causal class, no-endpoint inextendibility, parameter-counting Cauchy property and future-normal K convention are retained. The new complete-data development definition expressly adds model equations and matter data beyond the earlier stress-projection vocabulary.

The field law remains an adopted physical premise only in the physics packaging. Scalar and fluid formulas match their definitions; the nonnegative dust extension is explicitly defined locally rather than attributed to the positive-density definition.

Normal inverse maps, causal-cone and length statements, compact causal structure, choice premises and complete temporal flow are used at their stated scope. Eventual-domain limits are supported by the supplier's explicit step 7.1; its Statement wording is separately alerted.

Geodesic uniqueness, smooth exponential domains, connection transport and constant affine causal character are mathematical inputs. No physical free-fall postulate is used to justify a mathematical result.
Minkowski slices are used as Cauchy surfaces under the supplied absolutely continuous curve and choice conventions; flatness and causal reachability are consistent.
Straight affine geodesics and exponential maps are used correctly. Surjectivity of the Minkowski embedding is proved through complete straight-line lifts and target geodesic uniqueness.
The examples consistently use η=−dt²+|dx|² and future orientation ∂t, with spacelike level surfaces and data-fixing translations.
The separation and exponential constructions specialize correctly to Minkowski space. The translated rational tangent-ball family becomes exactly the rational-center Euclidean ball family.
